metadata.title: The density Turán problem for hypergraphs

nodes.name: Neighbourhood, degree, and maximum degree
nodes.statement: For $v \in V(H)$ in a $k$-graph $H$, $\Gamma_H(v)=\{B\in \binom{V(H)}{k-1}\mid \{v\}\cup B\in E(H)\}$; the degree of $v$ is $|\Gamma_H(v)|$ and $\Delta(H)=\max_v |\Gamma_H(v)|$.

nodes.name: Maximum disjoint degree $\Delta_0$
nodes.statement: $\Delta_0(H)=\max_{v\in V(H)}\{j\mid \text{there exist pairwise disjoint } B_1,\ldots,B_j\in \Gamma(v)\}$. Note $\Delta_0(H)\leq \Delta(H)$ with equality for all $2$-graphs and linear $k$-graphs.

nodes.name: Complete blow-up $\hat{H}$ and complete $n$-blow-up $\hat{H}(n)$
nodes.statement: $\hat{H}$ is formed from $H$ by replacing each $v\in V(H)$ by a non-empty class $A_v$ and taking edges to be all $k$-tuples from $k$ classes corresponding to an edge of $H$. If every class has size $n$ this is $\hat{H}(n)$.

nodes.name: Blow-up and $n$-blow-up of $H$
nodes.statement: A blow-up of $H$ is any subgraph $G\subseteq \hat{H}$. An $n$-blow-up is a subgraph $G\subseteq \hat{H}(n)$ with $V(G)=V(\hat{H}(n))$.

nodes.name: $H$-transversal and $H$-free blow-up
nodes.statement: An $H$-transversal is a subgraph isomorphic to $H$ with exactly one vertex from each vertex class $A_v$. A blow-up is $H$-free if it does not contain an $H$-transversal.

nodes.name: Edge density $d_e(G)$ and minimum density $d(G)$
nodes.statement: For $G\subseteq \hat{H}$ and $e\in E(H)$, $d_e(G)=|E(G[e])|/\prod_{v_i\in e}a_i$ where $G[e]$ is the $k$-partite subgraph induced by $\bigcup_{v_i\in e}A_i$; $d(G)=\min_{e\in E(H)} d_e(G)$.

nodes.name: Critical edge density $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)$
nodes.statement: $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)=\sup\{d(G)\mid G \text{ is an } H\text{-free blow-up of } H\}$. For disconnected $H$ this equals the maximum over components, so $H$ is assumed connected.

nodes.name: Partial $m$-Dyck path
nodes.statement: A path in the upper half-plane of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ from $(0,0)$ using rise steps $\uparrow=(1,1)$ and $m$-fall steps $\downarrow_m=(1,-m)$. The $y$-coordinate is the level; the height is the maximum level reached.

nodes.name: Full $m$-Dyck path, length, and maximum descent
nodes.statement: A partial $m$-Dyck path ending on the horizontal axis is a full $m$-Dyck path. Its length is the number of steps; a maximum descent is a longest sequence of consecutive $m$-falls.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{D}_m(s,l,h,d)$
nodes.statement: The set of partial $m$-Dyck paths ending at $(s,l)$, with height bounded by $h$ and maximum descent at most $d$. A `$\cdot$' argument removes the corresponding bound.

nodes.name: Projection $\pi_H$ and index map $\mathrm{ind}_i$
nodes.statement: For an $n$-blow-up $G$ of $H$, define $\pi_H:V(G)\to[h]$ by $\pi_H(w_j^i)=i$ and $\mathrm{ind}_i:A_i\to[n]$ by $\mathrm{ind}_i(w_j^i)=j$. For $P\subseteq V(G)$ and $e\in E(H)$, $P(e)=P\cap \bigcup_{i\in e}A_i$.

nodes.name: Partial $H$-transversal
nodes.statement: $P\subseteq V(G)$ such that (i) $|P\cap A_i|\leq 1$ for $1\leq i\leq h$, and (ii) for every $e\in E(H)$ with $e\subseteq \pi_H(P)$, $P(e)\in E(G)$.

nodes.name: Skeleton $H_2$ and tree operation $T\oplus_v f$
nodes.statement: The skeleton $H_2$ has $V(H_2)=V(H)$ and $xy\in E(H_2)$ iff some $e\in E(H)$ contains both $x$ and $y$. For a tree $T\subseteq H_2$ and $f\in E(H)$ meeting $T$ at single leaf $v$, $T\oplus_v f$ adds each $w\in f\setminus\{v\}$ as a leaf with parent $v$. $\mathrm{minleaf}(T)$ is the smallest leaf.

nodes.name: Bondy et al. (2006): critical edge density of $K_3$
nodes.statement: The triangle $K_3$ has critical edge density $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(K_3)=\varphi\approx 0.618\ldots$, the golden ratio.

nodes.name: Csikvári--Nagy (2012) bound for graphs
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and $t(H)$ is the largest root of its matching polynomial, then $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\leq 1-1/t(H)^2$ and in particular $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\leq 1-1/(4(\Delta-1))$.
assumptions: $H$ is a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$
$t(H)$ is the largest root of the matching polynomial of $H$

nodes.name: Markström--Thomassen (2019) for $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$
nodes.statement: For $k\geq 3$, the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph of order $k+1$ has $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(K_{k+1}^{(k)})=k/(k+1)$.

nodes.name: Main upper bounds on $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)$ (Theorem 4)
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a $k$-graph of order $h$ with max degree $\Delta$ and max disjoint degree $\Delta_0$. There exists $\alpha=\alpha(k,\Delta_0)$ with $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\leq 1-1/(\alpha\Delta)$. If $H$ is not $\Delta$-regular there also exists $\beta(k,h)$ with $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\leq 1-1/(\beta(\Delta-1))$. Both $\alpha,\beta\leq k(k/(k-1))^{k-1}<ke$.

nodes.name: Bounds for complete $k$-graphs $K_{k+l}^{(k)}$ (Theorem 5)
nodes.statement: If $1\leq l<k$ then $1-1/\Delta\leq d_{\mathrm{crit}}(K_{k+l}^{(k)})\leq 1-1/((l+1)\Delta)$.

nodes.name: Lower bound from finite optimisation (Proposition 6)
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a $k$-graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ then $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\geq 1-1/\Delta$.

nodes.name: Reduction to full $m$-Dyck paths (Lemma 7)
nodes.statement: For integers $h\geq m$ and $s,d,l\geq 1$ with $\max\{d,m\}\geq 2$, there exists $t\leq \lfloor (s+4h)/(m+1)\rfloor$ such that $|\mathcal{D}_m(s,l,h,d)|\leq |\mathcal{D}_m(t(m+1),0,h,d)|$.

nodes.name: Exponential bound on full $m$-Dyck paths with bounded descent (Lemma 8)
nodes.statement: For integers $m,t,d\geq 1$ with $\max\{d,m\}\geq 2$, let $\phi(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d x^{mi}$ and $\tau$ the unique positive solution of $\phi(x)=x\phi'(x)$. With $\alpha(m,d)=(\phi'(\tau))^m$, there exists $c_a=c_a(m,d)$ with $|\mathcal{D}_m(t(m+1),0,\cdot,d)|\leq c_a\alpha^t$, and $\alpha\leq \gamma_m=(m+1)(1+1/m)^m$.
assumptions: $\tau$ is the unique positive solution of $\phi(x)=x\phi'(x)$

nodes.name: Exponential bound on $m$-Dyck paths of bounded height (Lemma 9)
nodes.statement: For integers $h,m,t\geq 1$, let $\beta(m,h)$ be the reciprocal of the smallest root of $\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor (h+1)/(m+1)\rfloor} (-x)^i \binom{h-mi+1}{i}$. There is $c_b=c_b(m,h)$ with $|\mathcal{D}_m(t(m+1),0,h,\cdot)|\leq c_b\beta^t$. Moreover $\beta(1,h)=4\cos^2(\pi/(h+2))$.
assumptions: $\beta(m,h)$ is the reciprocal of the smallest root of $\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor (h+1)/(m+1)\rfloor} (-x)^i \binom{h-mi+1}{i}$

nodes.name: Lemma 8 of Esperet--Parreau (cited)
nodes.statement: Asymptotic enumeration of $1$-Dyck paths with allowed descent set $E$ via the equation $\phi_E(x)=x\phi_E'(x)$, used to bound the number of such paths by $c_E\alpha^t$ where $\alpha=(\phi_E'(\tau))$.
conclusions: The number of $1$-Dyck paths of given length with descents in $E$ is at most $c_E\alpha^t$
nodes.origin_citation: Esperet and Parreau, Lemma 8 [EsperetParreau]; also Drmota [Drmota]

nodes.name: Pétréolle et al. generating function (cited Proposition 2.3)
nodes.statement: For polynomials $g_j(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor(h-j)/(m+1)\rfloor}(-x)^i\binom{h-j-mi}{i}$ satisfying $g_k(x)-g_{k-1}(x)=xg_{k+m}(x)$ for $0\leq k\leq h-m$ (and $0$ otherwise), $g_0(x)/g_{-1}(x)$ is the ordinary generating function for $m$-Dyck paths of height bounded by $h$.
conclusions: $g_0(x)/g_{-1}(x)$ is the OGF for $m$-Dyck paths of height $\leq h$

nodes.name: Cauchy--Hadamard theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: The asymptotic growth rate of the coefficients of a power series equals the reciprocal of the radius of convergence.
assumptions: Power series with radius of convergence $R$

nodes.name: Density assumption for Algorithm (A) bound
nodes.statement: $d(G)\geq 1-\frac{1}{\alpha\Delta}+\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon>0$ where $\alpha=\alpha(k-1,\Delta_0)$.

nodes.name: Counting bound on $(r_t)$ via Algorithm (A)
nodes.statement: $h\,c_a(n+1)^h\,\alpha^{4h/k}\,(\Delta\alpha(1-d(G))n^k)^{s/k}\geq n^s$.

nodes.name: Counting bound on $(r_t)$ via Algorithm (B)
nodes.statement: $h\,c_b(n+1)^h\,\beta^{4h/k}\,((\Delta-1)\beta(1-d(G))n^k)^{s/k}\geq n^s$.

nodes.name: Algorithm (A): entropy-compression $H$-transversal search (general)
nodes.statement: Greedy/backtracking search for an $H$-transversal in an $n$-blow-up $G$ of $H$, consuming integers $z_t\in[n]$ to pick a vertex from class $A_{i_t}$ where $i_t$ is the smallest unrepresented vertex of $H$; on bad-edge violation it removes the offending vertices and records the violating edge.
output: An $H$-transversal $P_{t-1}$ in $G$ if the algorithm halts
Record sequence $(r_t)_{t=1}^s$ and final partial transversal $P_s$ from which $(z_t)$ can be reconstructed

nodes.name: Algorithm (B): tree-guided $H$-transversal search (non-regular case)
nodes.statement: Variant of Algorithm (A) using a spanning tree $T$ of the skeleton $H_2$ to choose the next vertex class $i_t=\mathrm{minleaf}(T_{t-1})$, with tree updates via $T\setminus\{i_t\}$ on success and $T\oplus_{i_t}\pi_H(P_t(e))$ on a bad-edge restart.
input: $T$ a spanning tree of the skeleton $H_2$
output: An $H$-transversal $P_{t-1}$ in $G$ if the algorithm halts
Record sequence $(r_t)_{t=1}^s$ and final partial transversal $P_s$ from which $(z_t)$ can be reconstructed

nodes.name: Density Turán problem for hypergraphs
nodes.statement: Determine the minimal value $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)$ such that any subgraph $G\subseteq \hat{H}$ with $d_e(G)>d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)$ for every $e\in E(H)$ contains an $H$-transversal.

nodes.name: Counting partial $m$-Dyck paths with bounded height/descent
nodes.statement: Estimate $|\mathcal{D}_m(s,l,h,d)|$, the number of partial $m$-Dyck paths ending at $(s,l)$ with height $\leq h$ and maximum descent $\leq d$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6 (lower bound)
nodes.statement: Generalisation to $k$-graphs of Corollary 3.8 of Nagy [nagy].

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7 (Dyck-path extension)
nodes.statement: Construct an injection from $\mathcal{D}_m(s,l,h,d)$ to $\mathcal{D}_m(t(m+1),0,h,d)$ by appending at most $4h$ rises and $m$-falls to extend each path to a full $m$-Dyck path while preserving height and descent bounds.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8 (bounded descent)
nodes.statement: Convert full $m$-Dyck paths with $t$ $m$-falls and max descent $d$ into $1$-Dyck paths of length $2tm$ with descents in $E=\{m,2m,\ldots,dm\}$, then apply Lemma 8 of Esperet--Parreau.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9 (bounded height)
nodes.statement: Use the weighted-Dyck-path generating function machinery of Pétréolle et al. with weights $\alpha_i=1$ for $i\leq h$ and $0$ otherwise; the Cauchy--Hadamard theorem gives the growth rate as the reciprocal of the smallest root of $g_{-1}(x)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4 (main bounds)
nodes.statement: Assume for contradiction $G$ is $H$-free with the claimed density. Run Algorithm (A) (resp.\ (B)); show the record $(r_t)$ corresponds to a partial $(k-1)$-Dyck path and bound the number of records using Lemmas 7--9, contradicting the reconstruction count $n^s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5 (complete $k$-graphs)
nodes.statement: Use Algorithm (A) and the exact count $(l+1)^t$ for partial $(k-1)$-Dyck paths of length $tk+k-1$ bounded by height $k+l-1$, then conclude as in the proof of Theorem 4.

nodes.name: Recovery of Csikvári--Nagy bound for $k=2$
nodes.statement: For $k=2$, $\beta\leq 4\cos^2(\pi/(h+1))$ and so Theorem 4 recovers the bound $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\leq 1-1/(4(\Delta-1))$ of Csikvári--Nagy when $H$ is not regular.

nodes.name: Entropy-compression methodology
nodes.statement: The proofs use the entropy compression technique of Moser--Tardos; the search algorithm doubles as a compression algorithm for integer sequences, leading to a contradiction when the blow-up is sufficiently dense.

nodes.name: Set up: assume contradiction with density bound
nodes.statement: Assume $G$ is $H$-free with $d(G)\geq 1-1/(\alpha\Delta)+\epsilon$ where $\alpha=\alpha(k-1,\Delta_0)$.

nodes.name: Define projection and partial transversal
nodes.statement: Define $\pi_H$, $\mathrm{ind}_i$, and partial $H$-transversal $P\subseteq V(G)$.

nodes.name: Run Algorithm (A) on the assumed sequence
nodes.statement: Run Algorithm (A) on $H$, $G$, and $(z_t)_{t=1}^\infty$. Since $G$ is $H$-free, the algorithm never halts.

nodes.name: Reconstruct $(z_t)$ from $(P_s,(r_t))$
nodes.statement: By forward induction reconstruct $(i_t),(\pi_H(P_t))$ from $(r_t)$, then by reverse induction recover $(z_t)$ and $(P_t)$ from $(P_s,(r_t))$. Hence at least $n^s$ distinct $(P_s,(r_t))$ are possible.

nodes.name: Map $(r_t)$ to a partial $(k-1)$-Dyck path
nodes.statement: Form $(r_t^\circ)$ tracking $|P_t|$: rise if $r_t=1$, $(k-1)$-fall if $r_t=P_t(e)$. This is a partial $(k-1)$-Dyck path of length $s$ with height $\leq h-1$ and max descent $\leq \Delta_0$.

nodes.name: Bound preimages of each Dyck path
nodes.statement: For each $(k-1)$-fall there are at most $\Delta(1-d(G))n^k$ choices for $r_t$ (edge times missing $k$-tuple); rises have a single preimage. With $\leq s/k$ falls this gives $(\Delta(1-d(G))n^k)^{s/k}$ preimages per path.

nodes.name: Apply Lemmas 7 and 8 to bound number of paths
nodes.statement: Lemmas 7 and 8 imply the number of valid $(r_t)$ is at most $h\,c_a\alpha^{(s+4h)/k}\,(\Delta(1-d(G))n^k)^{s/k}$.

nodes.name: Combine with $|P_s|<(n+1)^h$ and conclude contradiction
nodes.statement: Combining with $\leq (n+1)^h$ choices for $P_s$ gives $hc_a(n+1)^h\alpha^{4h/k}(\Delta\alpha(1-d(G))n^k)^{s/k}\geq n^s$, which under $1-d(G)\leq 1/(\alpha\Delta)-\epsilon$ fails for large $s,n$.

nodes.name: Tree-based variant for non-regular $H$ (Algorithm (B))
nodes.statement: Replace Algorithm (A) by Algorithm (B), using a spanning tree $T$ of the skeleton $H_2$ and reordering so vertex $h$ has degree $\leq \Delta-1$.

nodes.name: Tree variant: $\leq \Delta-1$ choices per fall
nodes.statement: When the leaf $i_t$ has a parent $p$ in $T_{t-1}$, the relevant edges $e\ni i_t$ with $p\notin e$ number at most $\Delta-1$; the case $i_t=h$ also gives at most $\Delta-1$ choices.

nodes.name: Apply Lemmas 7 and 9 and conclude second bound
nodes.statement: Using Lemmas 7 and 9 with $\beta=\beta(k-1,h-1)$ obtain $hc_b(n+1)^h\beta^{4h/k}((\Delta-1)\beta(1-d(G))n^k)^{s/k}\geq n^s$, impossible for $s,n$ large under $1-d(G)\leq 1/(\beta(\Delta-1))-\epsilon$.

nodes.name: $m\geq 2$ extension
nodes.statement: For $m\geq 2$, append $\uparrow^{h-l}$ rises, then $(\downarrow_m\uparrow)^j$ where $j=\lfloor h/(m-1)\rfloor$, then $\uparrow^{m-l_0}\downarrow_m$ if needed, using $\leq 4h$ extra steps and producing a full path of height $\leq h$.

nodes.name: $m=1$ extension
nodes.statement: For $m=1$, append $\uparrow^{h-l}$ then $(\downarrow^2\uparrow)^{h-2}\downarrow^2$, using $d\geq 2$, giving a full $1$-Dyck path with $\leq 4h$ extra steps.

nodes.name: Verify height and descent are preserved
nodes.statement: In each case the extension never exceeds height $h$ and the maximum descent remains $\leq d$, yielding the injection.

nodes.name: Bound $\alpha\leq \gamma_m$
nodes.statement: Note that $\gamma_m=\alpha(m,\infty)$, the value of $\alpha$ obtained by setting $d=\infty$, hence $\alpha(m,d)\leq \gamma_m$.

nodes.name: Convert to $1$-Dyck paths with descent set $E$
nodes.statement: Replace each $m$-fall by $m$ consecutive $1$-falls; full $m$-Dyck paths with $t$ $m$-falls and max descent $d$ become $1$-Dyck paths of length $2tm$ with descents from $E=\{m,2m,\ldots,dm\}$.

nodes.name: Apply Esperet--Parreau Lemma 8
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 8 of Esperet--Parreau with $\phi_E(x)=\sum_{i=0}^d x^{mi}$ to get a constant $c_E$ with at most $c_E\alpha^t$ such paths; set $c_a(m,d)=c_E$.

nodes.name: Define polynomials $g_j(x)$ and verify recurrence
nodes.statement: Define $g_j(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor(h-j)/(m+1)\rfloor}(-x)^i\binom{h-j-mi}{i}$ for $j\geq -1$ and verify $g_k-g_{k-1}=xg_{k+m}$ for $0\leq k\leq h-m$, and $0$ for $k>h-m$.

nodes.name: Identify $g_0/g_{-1}$ as the OGF
nodes.statement: By Proposition 2.3 of Pétréolle et al., $g_0(x)/g_{-1}(x)$ is the OGF for $m$-Dyck paths of height $\leq h$.

nodes.name: Apply Cauchy--Hadamard
nodes.statement: By Cauchy--Hadamard the growth rate is the reciprocal of the radius of convergence, which equals the smallest root of $g_{-1}(x)$; the special value $\beta(1,h)=4\cos^2(\pi/(h+2))$ comes from de Bruijn et al.

nodes.name: Exact count of partial $(k-1)$-Dyck paths for $K_{k+l}^{(k)}$
nodes.statement: For $H=K_{k+l}^{(k)}$, partial $(k-1)$-Dyck paths of length $tk+k-1$ bounded by height $k+l-1$ start with $k-1$ rises, then within the next $l+1$ steps one is a $(k-1)$-fall, and the path returns to level $k-1$ via rises; total count is $(l+1)^t$.

nodes.name: Conclude as in Theorem 4
nodes.statement: Plug $(l+1)^t$ into the entropy-compression bookkeeping of Algorithm (A) to obtain $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(K_{k+l}^{(k)})\leq 1-1/((l+1)\Delta)$.

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement: $P_0\leftarrow \emptyset$, $t\leftarrow 1$.

nodes.name: Outer while: $P_{t-1}$ not an $H$-transversal
nodes.statement: While $P_{t-1}$ is not an $H$-transversal, set $i_t\leftarrow \min([h]\setminus \pi_H(P_{t-1}))$.

nodes.name: Inner while: try to fill class $i_t$
nodes.statement: While $i_t\notin \pi_H(P_{t-1})$: $P_t\leftarrow P_{t-1}\cup\{w^{i_t}_{z_t}\}$.

nodes.name: Branch on whether $P_t$ is a partial $H$-transversal
nodes.statement: If $P_t$ is a partial $H$-transversal: $r_t\leftarrow 1$. Else choose $e\in E(H)$ with $e\subseteq \pi_H(P_t)$ and $P_t(e)\notin E(G)$, set $r_t\leftarrow P_t(e)$, $P_t\leftarrow P_t\setminus P_t(e)$, $i_{t+1}\leftarrow i_t$.

nodes.name: Increment and continue
nodes.statement: $t\leftarrow t+1$ and continue inner/outer loops.

nodes.name: Output $H$-transversal
nodes.statement: Output $P_{t-1}$ and halt.

nodes.name: Initialize tree-based search
nodes.statement: $P_0\leftarrow \emptyset$, $T_0\leftarrow T$, $t\leftarrow 1$.

nodes.name: Outer while: pick smallest leaf
nodes.statement: While $P_{t-1}$ is not an $H$-transversal: $i_t\leftarrow \mathrm{minleaf}(T_{t-1})$ and $P_t\leftarrow P_{t-1}\cup\{w^{i_t}_{z_t}\}$.

nodes.name: Branch on partial-transversal test
nodes.statement: If $P_t$ is a partial $H$-transversal: $r_t\leftarrow 1$, $T_t\leftarrow T_{t-1}\setminus\{i_t\}$. Else choose $e\in E(H)$ with $e\subseteq \pi_H(P_t)$ and $P_t(e)\notin E(G)$, set $r_t\leftarrow P_t(e)$, $T_t\leftarrow T_{t-1}\oplus_{i_t}\pi_H(P_t(e))$, $P_t\leftarrow P_t\setminus P_t(e)$.

nodes.name: Increment $t$
nodes.statement: $t\leftarrow t+1$ and continue.

nodes.name: Output $H$-transversal
nodes.statement: Output $P_{t-1}$ and halt.
